title: Tissue Clearing and Expansion for Multiscale Anatomy
content: The synergy between tissue clearing and selective plane illumination microscopy (SPIM) has blossomed over the past decade. Advancements in technology and methodology on both ends have led to this pairing becoming a more standard imaging practice in research laboratories [1, 2]. Tissue clearing involves matching the refractive index of a specimen with an imaging medium to minimize light scattering; SPIM exploits these optically uniform specimens to achieve volumetric imaging of thick or intact tissues.
